findings.text: The declared negative control is not performed. The done_when and the plan's §2 Negative control both require that a derivation keyed on process age reads the ten-day-old process as lost so the live case fails; here no process carrying session-long-lived is ever started (the fixture at :159-173 takes only `home` and renews a lease sixty seconds old), and the 'control' is `keyed_on_process_age = (NOW - ten_days_ago).total_seconds() > 72 * HOUR` followed by `assert keyed_on_process_age is True` -- arithmetic over the test's own literal NOW, which is true whatever the code does. A derivation that keyed on process age would find no process for this session, fall back to the same fresh lease, and still read live, so the assertion at :171 cannot redden on the regression the control names. negative-control.log repeats the same fiction, printing 'process-age derivation: lost = True' for a comparison no code computed. The gate's central discrimination claim therefore rests on an assertion whose two sides move together.

The case 'the setting moves the boundary' passes after_hours= directly to session_lost, so the flight-setting path the deliverable rests on -- lost_session_after_hours resolving lost_session.after_hours through flight.resolve() at reckon/crew/lost_sessions.py:42-57 -- is only ever exercised at its default. A regression that stopped reading the flight layer and always returned DEFAULT_AFTER_HOURS would leave all six cases green, so the schema, defaults and generated model this change adds are unverified by any test.

The admit pass computes result['lost_sessions'] outside any _read_tally block, so the 'lost-session reads' row added to service.py's _READ_SOURCES is never emitted by a production pass: neither admit_once nor its service callers at service.py:470 and :536 open a tally around it. The commit message's claim that 'its own receipt reports those reads under a named label so a later pass can show the bound holds' is true only of the test, which wraps admit_once in its own tally at tests/test_a_lost_session_is_a_derived_fact.py:218-219. The production receipt therefore cannot show the bound this node declares.

The schema admits after_hours = 0 (reckon/schema/flight.yaml's minimum_value: 0, the pydantic ge=0 at reckon/_flight_schema.py:759, and the JSON schema's minimum: 0), but lost_session_after_hours silently replaces any non-positive value with 72. A layer that sets 0 to mean 'anything unheard is lost' gets the shipped threshold instead, with no warning and no record of the override, so the declared setting and the value the derivation uses can disagree without either surface reporting it.

The commit carries ruff-format rewrites of pre-existing lines unrelated to the goal -- the result['released_plan_review'] call at :137-139, the _record_pass_hold and _verdict_row calls at :190-205, and an import reorder moving reckon.crew.open_run_index above the relative imports -- which the worker flags as a deviation. The repo's own rule is that a formatting sweep is its own commit, so this churn hides the intended change inside the one declared path a reviewer must read most closely.
